findings.measured: exec/stages/S4/review-runs/try-1794552515.log (27 of 230 requests carry 'Vary: Accept' on 7.2.4, all 27 sent an Accept header) and exec/stages/S4/review-runs/try-1794552582.log (through puma, GET /ip and POST /api/v1/send/message with 'Accept: */*')
findings.what: The Vary declaration says the application's responses carried no Vary header before. That is true only of requests that send no Accept header, which is what the recorded requests are. A request that sends one, as browsers, curl and HTTP libraries do, already got 'Vary: Accept' on 7.2.4 and gets 'Vary: Accept, X-Requested-With' on 8.0.5.2. For real traffic the change is one added field name, not a new header, so the sentence telling the client a cache 'will now keep separate copies per Accept' is wrong for those requests: it already did. The header on 8.0.5.2 is exactly what the stage declares, on every request we made, so nothing undeclared reaches a client. The declaration's 'before', the paragraph for the client and the question for the client need correcting.

Error entries in the Rails log change shape. On 7.2.4 an error with a cause is logged as the error line, its trace, then a 'Causes:' block naming the cause. On 8.0.5.2 the error line is followed by a 'Caused by:' line, then an 'Information for:' section with the trace, then an 'Information for cause:' section with the cause's trace. One class name in those entries changes too: a malformed query string is reported as ActionDispatch::ParameterTypeError where it was Rack::QueryParser::ParameterTypeError, because Action Pack 8.0 parses parameters itself. The responses are the same (400). It matters to anything that parses or alerts on this optional log.
findings.where: the Rails log, written only with LOGGING_RAILS_LOG_ENABLED=true

findings.what: The message of ActionController::ParameterMissing changes from 'param is missing or the value is empty: domain' to 'param is missing or the value is empty or invalid: domain'. No response carries it: the request answers 400 with an empty body on both versions. It appears in the exception_message field of Postal's own request log line, which is on by default, and in the Rails log. We did not capture what Sentry receives, but the same exception object goes there. It matters to a log search or an alert that matches the old text.
findings.where: config/initializers/logging.rb:8, Postal's own request log, and the Rails log

method.changelogs_note: 7 of 12 component changelogs for 8.0, 333 entries counting the 'No changes' lines. We read the first line of every entry and the full text of the ones that remove, rename, move or newly define something, and searched repo/ for each of those. The other five components (Active Job, Action Cable, Active Storage, Action Text, Action Mailbox) are not loaded by config/application.rb and were not read. Entries that apply. Action Pack: the Vary header (declared by the stage), Action Pack parsing request parameters itself (measured, 138 inputs parse the same on both versions), the SameSite change for session stores (cookie store here; cookie attributes measured the same), HEAD on error pages (measured the same on both versions), params.expect, which is where the new ParameterMissing message comes from (finding 3). Active Record: db:migrate on an empty database (declared; measured here), MySQL 5.5 dropped (in the stage's follow-ups). Active Support: to_time_preserves_timezone (the recorded deprecation warning; the setting reads true on 7.2.4 and :offset on 8.0.5.2, the same behavior). Railties: deferred route drawing (all 14 boots draw the routes when asked, the OIDC route included), secret_key_base in development and test (the code is the same in the installed 7.2.4 and 8.0.5.2). Active Model: the password reset token (fixed by the stage), confirmation validation of a blank password (the application passes validations: false; five password cases validate the same on both versions). Action View: rails-html-sanitizer 1.7.2 (the forced lock move). Searched and not used by the application: enum with keyword arguments, ConnectionPool#connection, ActiveSupport::ProxyObject, Benchmark.ms, config.read_encrypted_secrets, Rails::ConsoleMethods, form_with with a nil model, content passed to void tags, unsigned_float and unsigned_decimal, Rails content security policy (the application uses secure_headers).

upstream_diff.against: branch chore/rails-7-2-and-dependency-upgrades, branch upgrade-rails-8.1.4 and the project's open pull request for Rails 8.1
upstream_diff.why_not: None is a break this stage needed. The error message helper, its initializer and the stylesheet replace the dynamic_form gem, which is their choice: on 8.0.5.2 the gem loads and 27 invalid form posts render the same as on 7.2.4. The framework defaults files are their choice; this plan keeps load_defaults at 7.0 and adopts defaults in a later stage. The explicit YAML coder on the two serialized columns is their choice: on 8.0.5.2 both columns still use the YAML coder and a value round trips. db/schema.rb is the version stamp, which the stage lists as a follow-up. The annotaterb task replaces annotate, which S2 removed. Their Gemfile adds benchmark for 8.1; on 8.0.5.2 Active Support still depends on it and the worker's Benchmark.realtime call ran. Their Gemfile pins json below 3; ours does not (finding 6). lib/migration_waiter.rb and config/environments/test.rb already carry their change from S3, and cgi is in the Gemfile from this stage.
